objective.statement: Give the red torus widget its own label, "Red Torus Widget", for both its visible text and its aria-label, so the two home page widgets have distinct accessible names.

complexity.rationale: One presentational component, behaviour and wording are explicit, the fault is localised to two string literals, and no approval boundary, contract or cross-feature change is involved. The fast path skips planning ceremony only; the failing test and review lenses still apply.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The red TorusWidget has aria-label "Red Torus Widget" and visible label text "Red Torus Widget".
The green TorusWidget (including the default no-props render) keeps aria-label "Torus Widget" and visible label text "Torus Widget".
HomeView exposes two torus widget regions with different accessible names: "Torus Widget" and "Red Torus Widget".
Colours, sizes (150px torus, 6px ring, widget no bigger than 200px by 200px) and the HomeView layout are unchanged.

in.statement: TorusWidget.tsx (per-colour label used for both the aria-label and the visible text) and the matching component tests in TorusWidget.component.test.tsx and HomeView.component.test.tsx.

out.statement: The green widget label, colours, sizes, HomeView layout, test ids, other components, dependencies, and historical workflow records.

observations.statement: TorusWidget.tsx hard-codes aria-label="Torus Widget" (line 22) and the visible text "Torus Widget" (line 53) for every colour. HomeView mounts <TorusWidget /> and <TorusWidget color="red" />, so both sections have the accessible name "Torus Widget".
TorusWidget already takes an optional color prop (green default, red). The label should follow that prop, so no new prop, dependency or external contract is needed.
No existing test asserts the red widget's label. Existing tests asserting "Torus Widget" render the default green widget and stay valid, so no existing test needs to change.
Implement the label as a per-colour constant next to TORUS_PALETTES, used for both aria-label and the visible text so they cannot drift apart. The e2e spec does not reference the torus widget.

increments.behavior: The red TorusWidget is labelled "Red Torus Widget" in both its aria-label and its visible text, while the green widget keeps "Torus Widget".
increments.doneWhen: The red-label component tests and the HomeView distinct-names test pass, and every existing test still passes unchanged.
